newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Aug 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Aug 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The auditor-general's report on the controversial 185 million rand Motheo rural housing project is expected to call for a forensic audit of the scheme while taking top-level Mpumalanga officials to task, according to documents.

- The African National Congress-led audit commission has backed Auditor-General Henri Kluever in the row between him and Mineral and Energy Minister Penuell Maduna. It is to obtain legal advice on whether Maduna was in breach of the constitution with his accusations against Kluever last week.

- The African National Congress's Gauteng general council was unable to elect a replacement for premier Tokyo Sexwale on Sunday, with leadership wrangles continuing well into the night after eight hours of deliberation.
- Industrial holding company Bidvest Group lifted attributable earnings 34.1 percent to 228,5 million rand in the year to June following strong performances from all its operating divisions.
- United Cricket Board of SA (UCB) MD Ali Bacher on Sunday denied allegations that there had been kickbacks of bribes in a multimillion-rand deal with cellular phone company MTN.
BUSINESS REPORT

- South African taxpayers are facing at least 16 possible new charges and levies in the near future, Raymond Parsons, the director-general of the South African Chamber of Business (Sacob), said last week.
- Traders on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange are expecting a turbulent session today after shares on New York's Wall Street and other international stock markets fell badly late on Friday.

- Bidvest, the distribution, services and trading group, surpassed analysts' optimistic expectations, reporting on Sunday a 25 percent surge in earnings from 105.6 cents in the previous year to 132.5 cents a share for the 12 months to June 30.

- Last week's defection of UAL Merchant Bank's entire project finance team to Capital Alliance, the financial services group headed by Mzi Khumalo, was a "relatively minor hiccup", Geoff Richardson, the deputy chairman of UAL, said at the weekend.
- Joining the "mile-high club" will be easy in a few years' time for some passengers flying from Johannesburg to London with Virgin Atlantic Airways.
SAKE BEELD
- South Africa's money matters are planned well but the state services are in a shamble and there is corruptions in the public sector.
- De Beers, the world's largest diamond producer, seizure programme took an ugly turn.
- Wall Street's bulky fall on Friday had investors all over the world on hold.
THE STAR

- South African soccer hit not only the sporting, but also the financial jackpot on Saturday when Bafana Bafana won a place in the World Cup finals in France next June for the first time in the country's history.
- Bafana Bafana earned their rightful place on the world foot-balling stage on Saturday - and the swarm of supporters celebrated in a colourful and ecstatic display of emotion.
- "Congo for lunch" read a message on the back of a taxi - and it was definitely Congo for Sunday lunch in some Soweto homes on Sunday.
